txn_value_ytd2026.note: composite: sales value + mortgage value; ~5bn gap vs those two components combined is unmodeled registration categories (gifts, initial off-plan registration, etc), hence the looser tolerance

sales_value_ytd2026.note: maps to SUM(transactions.price_aed) — this table models sales only, not mortgages

residential_sales_value_fy2025.note: maps to SUM(transactions.price_aed) WHERE property_type IN ('Apartment','Villa')

foreign_growth_share_fy2025.note: share of (txn_value_fy2025 - fy2024 total) attributable to buyer_origin='Foreign'; combined with foreign_share_baseline_pre2025 to derive the FY2025 foreign value share

txn_value_h1_2025.note: algebraically incompatible with the other windows at tight tolerance: last_12mo minus ytd_2026 pins Aug-Dec 2025 at ~110.9bn, while fy_2025 minus h1_2025 caps Jul-Dec 2025 at ~88bn total -- a direct contradiction between the live-dashboard-sourced anchors (txn_value_last12mo, sales_value_ytd2026) and this biannual-report-sourced figure, most likely a reporting-lag/revision gap between snapshot dates. The generator prioritizes the mutually-consistent five-window set (last_12mo, prior_12mo, fy_2024, fy_2025, ytd_2026, all exact) and leaves h1_2025 unraked/informational; tolerance widened accordingly rather than silently dropped. The residential-only +38% YoY figure is informational context only, not separately enforced.

rented_units_current.note: a stock (currently occupied units), not a flow; used as the average-monthly-stock target for rental_stock(idx), not a rental_contracts row-count target directly — see rental_turnover_rate

foreign_share_baseline_pre2025.note: modeling assumption, not an independently published figure: pre-2025 (FY2024 and earlier) baseline share of transaction value attributable to foreign buyers. Combined with foreign_growth_share_fy2025 to derive an FY2025 foreign value share and build a smooth foreign-buyer-share curve.

rental_turnover_rate.note: modeling assumption, not an independently published figure: fraction of currently-rented stock that generates a loggable new-or-renewal contract event in a given year. Translates the rented_units_current stock anchor into a row-generation flow rate for the rental_contracts event-log table, since this table is an aggregated-realistic sample (~700k rows over 7.5 years), not an exhaustive per-lease census.
